subject: sr-business-studies
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Identify the type of business environment: (a) Includes the set of laws and regulations which influence business organisations. (b) Includes methods, techniques and approaches for production of goods and services.
questions.answer: (a) Legal environment. (b) Technological environment.

questions.q: Identify the characteristic of a joint stock company: (a) Day-to-day management is done by elected representatives called the board of directors. (b) The company enjoys continuous existence.
questions.answer: (a) Distinct pattern of management. (b) Perpetual succession.

questions.q: Name the function of management: Alliance Ltd's departments coordinate and authority–responsibility relationships are established with clarity of reporting. (also give its importance)
questions.answer: Organising; it leads to specialisation and clarity of authority and responsibility.

questions.q: Name the process of finding and attracting suitable applicants; list two of its sources.
questions.answer: Recruitment; internal sources (transfer, promotion) and external sources (advertisements, employment exchanges).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Control looks back at ______ performance. (b) Control looks forward to ______ performance.
questions.answer: (a) past. (b) future.

questions.q: Give an example of current assets.
questions.answer: Cash, inventories, debtors or bills receivable (any one).

questions.q: (i) Debentures with no fixed time of redemption are called ______. (ii) The depository receipts issued by a USA-based bank for trading only in American stock markets are known as ______.
questions.answer: (i) Irredeemable (perpetual) debentures. (ii) American Depository Receipts (ADRs).

questions.q: Name the three functions of financial markets.
questions.answer: Price discovery, providing liquidity and reducing transaction costs.

questions.q: Name the channel of distribution in the following cases: (i) Sale of cars by Maruti through company-approved retailers. (ii) Sale of water purifiers by a company directly through its own sales staff.
questions.answer: (i) One stage channel. (ii) Zero stage channel.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Publicity is a paid form of communication. (ii) Salesmanship is personal selling.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: ______ refers to buying goods from the manufacturers or wholesalers and selling them to final consumers.
questions.answer: Retail trade.

questions.q: Expand: (i) IEC (ii) RCMC (iii) ECGC.
questions.answer: (i) Import Export Code. (ii) Registration-cum-Membership Certificate. (iii) Export Credit and Guarantee Corporation.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) An importer cannot import goods without a valid import licence. (b) The exporter pays the import duty.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – the importer (through the clearing agent) pays import duty.

questions.q: Which business is considered a 'Small Business'? Explain.
questions.answer: A business actively managed by its owners, operating in a local area and small in size; under MSMED Act 2006 manufacturing units with plant and machinery investment up to Rs 5 crore (services up to Rs 2 crore) are small enterprises.

questions.q: Identify in e-banking: (a) a card that allows spending up to the balance in the account; (b) a machine to withdraw money at convenience; (c) a system giving banking facility over the telephone; (d) accessing the account anytime, anywhere.
questions.answer: (a) Debit card. (b) ATM. (c) Telebanking. (d) Internet banking.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is meant by globalisation?
questions.answer: Integrating the economy of a country with the world economy through free flow of goods, services, capital, technology and labour across borders.

questions.q: State any two limitations of planning.
questions.answer: It leads to rigidity and does not work in a dynamic environment; it is time consuming and expensive.

questions.q: State any two factors affecting the choice of capital structure.
questions.answer: Cash flow position and cost of financing (also tax rate, return on investment and risk).

questions.q: Differentiate between advertising and sales promotion on any two bases.
questions.answer: Advertising is a paid, non-personal mass communication for long-term image; sales promotion offers short-term, temporary incentives to induce quick purchase.

questions.q: Explain visible and invisible trade.
questions.answer: Visible trade is import and export of goods; invisible trade is exchange of services such as shipping, insurance and tourism.

questions.q: What is e-Post?
questions.answer: A service in which printed or handwritten messages are sent as e-mail and printed, enveloped and delivered by the post office at the destination.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Give any three features of a private company.
questions.answer: Restricts the transfer of shares; limits members to 200 and needs minimum two; prohibits invitation to the public to subscribe to its securities (and adds 'Private Limited' to its name).

questions.q: State any three benefits of 'leadership'.
questions.answer: It influences behaviour towards organisational benefit, builds confidence and reduces wastage and builds morale and higher productivity.

questions.q: Explain any three points of significance of co-ordination.
questions.answer: It reconciles goals of different departments, avoids overlapping and conflict as size grows and ensures economy and efficiency.

questions.q: Explain any three merits of public deposits.
questions.answer: Simple and easy, no charge on assets and economical (also flexible).

questions.q: Explain the benefits of salesmanship to consumers.
questions.answer: The salesperson guides and informs the customer, explains how to use the product and gives after-sales information.

questions.q: Explain any three types of small business.
questions.answer: Micro enterprises, ancillary units supplying at least 50 per cent to another industry and cottage industries run by family members.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the importance of organising.
questions.answer: It leads to specialisation, optimum use of resources, clarity of authority, creativity, growth, coordination and adaptation to change.

questions.q: Explain the money market instruments with their maturity periods.
questions.answer: Call money (1 day to a fortnight), treasury bills (up to 364 days), commercial paper (15 days to one year), certificates of deposit (91 days to one year) and trade bills (within one year).

questions.q: Define a wholesaler and identify any four functions performed by them.
questions.answer: A wholesaler buys goods in bulk from manufacturers and sells to retailers. Functions: procurement of goods, grading and packing, transporting, warehousing, financing, risk bearing, market information and selling.

questions.q: Explain the applications of e-commerce.
questions.answer: E-banking, e-ticketing, e-advertising, e-trading at stock exchanges, computerised mail and e-Post, and online education.
